title: LiveRegion
summary: Telling a screen reader about a change without moving focus is a posted announcement on iOS, not a rendered region. Monarch ships nothing and uses the same call inside its components.
whenToUse: Post an announcement when something changes that the person did not directly cause or cannot see: a save finished, a result count changed, an error appeared, an item moved. For a value that changes continuously, add the updatesFrequently trait to the element instead.
whenNotToUse: Do not announce what VoiceOver already reads: the new value of the focused control, or a screen change. When a new screen or a large part of one appears, post AccessibilityNotification.ScreenChanged or LayoutChanged instead.
api: func accessibilityAddTraits(_ traits: AccessibilityTraits) -> some View

states.name: polite
states.description: The default priority. The announcement may be dropped if other speech interrupts it.

states.name: assertive
states.description: The high priority interrupts current speech. Keep it for errors and for the steps of a drag.

appearance: Nothing is drawn. If sighted people need the message too, show it with a banner or text as well.
platformNotes: The web renders an aria-live region and changes its text; the web component also offers a useAnnouncer hook. iOS has no live region: the app posts the announcement at the moment of the change. Android sets a live-region property on a composable instead. Monarch components that announce (the text field's error, the stop button's stopped state, the typing dots) call the same API.
accessibility: System behaviour: the announcement is spoken by VoiceOver and shown on a braille display without moving focus.
Nothing is spoken when no assistive technology is running; posting is always safe.
An element with the updatesFrequently trait is re-read at intervals while it has focus, instead of on every change.
edgeCases: An announcement posted in the same moment as a screen change is usually lost; post it after the transition.
The same text posted twice is spoken twice. No padding character is needed, unlike on the web.
The priority attribute needs the AttributedString form.
